quarterly_data.signal: 10-K fiscal 2026 (year ended June 30, 2026) results by product type and end market: revenue was $678,927 thousand versus $696,162 thousand (-2.5%); Power discrete $437,787 thousand (-2.6%), Power IC $233,870 thousand (+1.7%), packaging and testing services and other $7,270 thousand, license and development services nil (versus $13,841 thousand). By end market, Computing was $342,952 thousand (+5.8%), Communication $132,278 thousand (+6.8%), Consumer $83,008 thousand (-18.9%) and Power Supply and Industrial $113,419 thousand (-12.2%). Gross margin was 22.3% versus 23.1%; research and development expense was $103,858 thousand versus $94,265 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $678,927 thousand (-2.5%); Power discrete $437,787 thousand (-2.6%); Power IC $233,870 thousand (+1.7%); Computing $342,952 thousand (+5.8%); gross margin 22.3% (23.1%)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K customer concentration: AOS sells most of its products through distributors; its two largest distributors, WPG Holdings Limited and Promate Electronic Co. Ltd., accounted for 53.0% and 19.3% of revenue respectively in fiscal 2026 (51.3% and 22.1% in fiscal 2025; 46.0% and 25.0% in fiscal 2024), together 72.3%, 73.4% and 71.0%. The distributor agreements renew automatically for one-year periods unless terminated.

10-K named customers (list only, no figures): AOS says it has direct relationships with key OEMs including Dell Inc., Hewlett-Packard Company, Samsung Group and Stanley Black & Decker, most of whom it serves through its distributors and ODMs; its ODM customers include Compal Electronics, Foxconn, Quanta Computer, Wistron and Delta Electronics. AOS says it has released or is designing in several multiphase controller families serving Intel, AMD and NVIDIA, which it says has enabled it to become a complete solution level provider across PCs, graphics cards, AI and datacenter.

10-K product launches in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026: AOS unveiled a total power solution for next-generation Intel Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake platforms (variable-frequency hysteretic peak-current mode control with phase-current sensing) and launched the SmartClamp family of protected DrMOS, designed for the power demands of AI servers, data centers and high-end graphics cards, with high-accuracy over current protection and negative current protection.

10-K manufacturing and supply: AOS operates an 8-inch wafer fab in Hillsboro, Oregon and in-house packaging and testing facilities in Shanghai, China that handle most of its packaging and testing (the JV Company handles a portion); its facilities have the combined capacity to package and test over 600 million parts per month; wafers from third-party suppliers account for approximately 35% of total wafer supply. AOS holds an equity interest of approximately 18.9% (June 30, 2026) in the Chongqing JV Company (power semiconductor packaging, testing and 12-inch wafer fab), remains a major customer of it, and the JV Company has agreed to provide AOS a specified level of monthly wafer production capacity (a capacity guarantee subject to future increase). AOS is converting some products from gold to copper wire as gold prices rose and supply chain partners assess surcharges. Outstanding purchase commitments, primarily for semiconductor raw materials, wafers, spare parts and packaging and testing services, were approximately $63.6 million at June 30, 2026 versus $85.9 million a year earlier; purchases of property and equipment were $51,752 thousand in fiscal 2026 versus $37,180 thousand.
